minutes.headline: Charter Review Committee finished reading the draft charter and planned January votes and a February public hearing.
minutes.summary: The committee read through Articles 5 to 8 of the town charter. It discussed administrative reorganization, the fire chief section, school and town budget procedures, capital planning, and the rules for multiple member bodies, including quorum, ratification and removals. Finance sections were held for a January 10th session. Members set a timeline of a public hearing in February, action by late February, then Town Counsel review. No formal votes on charter language were taken.

what_happened.line: The Charter Review Committee proposed a February public hearing on the draft charter, with committee action a week later.
Members plan preliminary votes on charter language at the second meeting in January; no formal votes on charter language were taken at this meeting.
A member will draft proposed changes from the discussions and circulate them before the next meeting.
The committee read Articles 5 to 8, including the fire chief section, school and town budget procedures, capital planning, and quorum and removals.
Members confirmed that a supermajority requires six affirmative votes.

why_it_matters: The draft charter sets how the school and town budgets are made, including how Town Meeting votes on school money and how far ahead the town manager must project costs, so changes touch the budgets residents vote on.
The February hearing is the point where residents can comment on the draft before the committee acts and Town Counsel reviews it.
